pr_body:
The existing set_offline() short-circuit erroneously included
when f->archive was true and header->state was STATE_OFFLINE.

This commit makes the short-circuit f->archive aware, so it will
only catch scenarios where there's not an offlining in progress
and the header state matches the target state of either archived
or offline.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/17770
pr_comments: This is completely untested beyond "seems to compile", but appears obviously correct to me.

@poettering FYI of all the journal-related PRs I've posted as of late, this one is arguably the most important to verify/review... and is a small change, but does require scrutinizing the details.

In making this fix, I wondered if STATE_ARCHIVED should be renamed to STATE_OFFLINE_ARCHIVED to more clearly express archived as being handled as an offline variant, especially with all the "offlining" naming of the functions surrounding the fsync and switching of the header->state dance.  WDYT?

looks superficially good to me. To me the fact that "archived" is a special case of "offline" is kinda obvious. But I'd also be fine with renaming the state, up to you.

Did oyu give this any further testing?
No, I did not get around to testing this, and am a bit preoccupied atm dealing with a move.

issue_context.title: Archived journals don't reliably get header->state set to STATE_ARCHIVED
issue_context.body:
This one's probably my fault.

While developing/testing jio (https://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/systemd-devel/2020-November/045641.html) it became apparent my system has a significant number of archived user journals having header->state=STATE_OFFLINE.

I think the problem is if a journal's state is already STATE_OFFLINE, the offline+fsync machinery doesn't get triggered at all, which means it will just be left as STATE_OFFLINE, despite needing to be switched to STATE_ARCHIVED from offline.  Everything is predicated on header->state=STATE_ONLINE.

This is largely benign which is why it's gone ignored for so long, but we should fix it so operations like a potential future tail-waste truncation feature applicable only to STATE_ARCHIVED journals can actually include all eligible archived journals by reading their state as such.

Sample jio output highlighting the problem:

Note all those user-1000@... files are Offline, and their names are obviously post-archived, and uncorrupted.

As for why the *user* journal specificity, I presume it's because they're largely idle resulting in their state mostly being offline because of how systemd-journald keeps journals offline until there's more appends.
